title: Injector Cylinder 1 — Open Circuit
shortDescription: Fuel injector #1 electrical circuit open — coil or wiring fault.
fullDescription:
MID 128 is the Volvo engine ECM; PSID 18 refers to cylinder 1 injector open circuit fault on Volvo D11/D13/D16 engines in VN, VNL, and VHD trucks.

The ECM commanded injection but did not see the expected current flow. Most common root cause is a broken wire inside the valve cover harness — these age and crack over time with heat cycling. Sometimes the injector solenoid itself has failed.

Repair typically requires valve cover removal. Use dielectric grease on injector connectors during reassembly to prevent future corrosion.

causes.cause: Broken wire in valve cover harness

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Swap cyl 1 injector or harness pin with another cylinder. If fault moves, confirms injector or harness branch.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Under valve cover, inspect injector harness for broken strands, oil saturation, burn marks.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty part
fixSteps.instruction: Replace internal harness or injector. Use new valve cover gasket. Code injector trim with Volvo Tech Tool (VCADS/PTT).

whenToCallPro: If injector trim coding required — dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 injector 1 open circuit MID 128 PSID 18

faq.a: Volvo D13 injectors are typically reliable; harness fails more often.
Yes, new injector needs coding via Volvo Tech Tool.

title: DEF Dosing Valve Mechanical Failure
shortDescription: DEF doser valve stuck or not responding to commands.
fullDescription:
SPN 5394 on Volvo D11/D13/D16 indicates the DEF dosing valve (injector spraying DEF into exhaust pre-SCR) has a mechanical fault. FMI 7 means the valve did not reach commanded position.

Common cause: urea crystallization on the tip/pintle. DEF crystallizes when hot exhaust evaporates fluid; over time crystals jam the valve. Cleaning is sometimes possible; often replacement is needed.

Be aware: the DEF doser is exhaust-mounted and can reach 500°F+. Allow extended cooldown before service.

fixSteps.title: Cool engine
fixSteps.instruction: Allow exhaust to cool 60+ min before service.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean doser
fixSteps.instruction: Unbolt doser. Soak tip in warm distilled water to dissolve crystals. Rinse.

fixSteps.title: Test or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test coil resistance. If open or cleaning didn't fix, replace doser. Re-prime via Volvo Tech Tool.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 DEF doser SPN 5394 crystallization clean

faq.a: Quality DEF + avoid excess idle. Some is unavoidable.
Yes — only for dissolving crystals, fully dry before reinstall.

title: DEF Quality Severely Poor
shortDescription: DEF quality well below spec — severe contamination or wrong fluid.
fullDescription:
SPN 3364 FMI 1 on Volvo trucks means DEF urea concentration is severely off-spec (most-severe severity). Often the result of diesel or water contaminating the DEF tank, or non-certified fluid added.

If diesel entered the DEF tank — do NOT start the engine. Tow to dealer. Diesel in DEF destroys the $6,000+ SCR catalyst when it reaches the doser.

Water contamination is more recoverable: drain, flush, refill with fresh API-certified DEF, re-check with refractometer.

fixSteps.title: If diesel contamination: DO NOT START
fixSteps.instruction: Tow to dealer immediately. Starting spreads contamination to doser and SCR.

fixSteps.title: Drain and flush DEF
fixSteps.instruction: Pump out tank, flush with fresh DEF 2-3 times until refractometer shows 32.5%.

fixSteps.title: Test SCR function
fixSteps.instruction: With Volvo Tech Tool, run SCR diagnostic. If efficiency codes persist, SCR damaged — dealer replacement.

whenToCallPro: If diesel contamination or SCR damage.
videoSearchQuery: Volvo VNL DEF contamination SPN 3364 flush

faq.q: Diesel in DEF tank — how bad?
faq.a: $6,000+ SCR replacement if you start the engine.
DEF cap should seal — replace if loose.

title: Inlet NOx Slightly High
shortDescription: Engine-out NOx above target — early sign of combustion or EGR issue.
fullDescription:
SPN 3216 FMI 15 (least severe) on Volvo D11/D13/D16 flags engine-out NOx slightly above expected. Often indicates EGR not flowing enough (stuck valve, sooted venturi), or NOx sensor drifting.

Check EGR operation first via Volvo Tech Tool — commanded vs actual position. Clean EGR or replace valve as needed. If EGR is healthy, sensor may be drifting and needs replacement.

Untreated this escalates to SPN 4364 SCR efficiency and derate.

fixSteps.title: Command EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Via Volvo Tech Tool, command EGR 0-100%. Verify actual tracks. Sticking = clean or replace.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Pull EGR valve and clean carbon with intake cleaner and brass brush.

fixSteps.title: Replace inlet NOx sensor if EGR OK
fixSteps.instruction: If EGR passes test, replace aging inlet NOx sensor.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 inlet NOx high EGR SPN 3216

faq.a: Prevents escalation to derate and keeps SCR from poisoning from bad inputs.
Actuate EGR first — faster test, more common root cause.

title: Crankcase Pressure High (CCV Fault)
shortDescription: Crankcase ventilation / blow-by pressure excessive — possible worn rings or CCV filter plugged.
fullDescription:
Volvo MID 128 PSID 230 monitors crankcase pressure via sensor in the CCV (crankcase vent) system. High reading indicates either a plugged CCV filter/separator or excessive blow-by from worn piston rings/cylinder liners.

On Volvo D13, the CCV filter (round cartridge on engine top) is a 200,000-mile service item. Skipped service causes oil mist to back up and set this code.

If CCV filter is clean and new, and pressure remains high, a compression test or leak-down is warranted — may indicate early ring wear.

fixSteps.title: Replace CCV filter
fixSteps.instruction: Volvo CCV filter at top of engine. Replace cartridge with OEM filter per service interval.

fixSteps.title: Clear and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Clear code with Volvo Tech Tool. Run a drive cycle — code should not return.

fixSteps.title: Compression/leakdown if persists
fixSteps.instruction: If new filter doesn't fix, dealer performs compression test to assess ring/liner wear.

whenToCallPro: If ring wear suspected — overhaul territory.
videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 CCV filter replace MID 128 PSID 230

faq.a: Typically every 200,000 miles — check Volvo maintenance schedule.

title: VGT Vanes Not Reaching Commanded Position
shortDescription: Variable geometry turbo vanes stuck with soot or mechanical fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 641 FMI 7 on Volvo D11/D13/D16 trucks means the VGT vanes are not moving to the commanded position — the ECM commands and the position feedback differs.

Primary cause: carbon/soot binding the vanes. Running Volvo trucks under light load (short-haul, lots of idle) accelerates carbon accumulation. Schedule VGT cleaning at 400,000-600,000 miles, or at this code.

VGT replacement is significant labor — $4,000-$5,000 typically. Cleaning first is worth trying.

fixSteps.title: Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Run VGT calibration via Volvo Tech Tool — may free slightly stuck vanes.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean turbo
fixSteps.instruction: Turbo removal, soak center section in solvent, free vanes, reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Replace turbo if seized
fixSteps.instruction: Swap VGT assembly. Recalibrate after install.

whenToCallPro: Complex turbo job — dealer or diesel specialist.
videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 VGT stuck SPN 641 FMI 7 clean

faq.a: Avoid extended idle, run highway regularly, maintain EGR.
About 60% of stuck VGTs recover with solvent soak.

title: Coolant Temp Slightly Above Normal
shortDescription: Coolant temp entering warning zone — early overheat warning.
fullDescription:
SPN 110 FMI 15 on Volvo VN/VNL is the earliest overheat warning — temperature above normal but below derate threshold (typically 210-225°F). Easy-to-fix causes dominate at this stage.

Inspect radiator/CAC for debris, check coolant level, and verify fan clutch operation. Fix now to prevent progression to FMI 16 (derate) and FMI 0 (shutdown).

Volvo D13 is sensitive to coolant system air pockets — always bleed thoroughly after service.

fixSteps.title: Check coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Cold-engine check in surge tank. Top off with 50/50 pre-mix. Bleed air per Volvo procedure.

fixSteps.title: Clean radiator
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse radiator/CAC fins with garden hose. Remove bugs/debris.

fixSteps.title: Fan and thermostat test
fixSteps.instruction: Command fan ON via Tech Tool. If doesn't engage, replace clutch. Test thermostat by feeling upper hose during warmup.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo VNL overheat SPN 110 FMI 15 diagnose

faq.a: D13 traps air easily — can cause hot spot and false gauge reading.
Fix now at FMI 15 to avoid FMI 16 derate later.

title: Accelerator Pedal Data Link Fault
shortDescription: Throttle pedal position data not received via J1939 at expected rate.
fullDescription:
SPN 974 FMI 9 on Volvo trucks indicates the ECM is not receiving accelerator pedal position messages at the expected rate over the J1939 bus. This is typically a dash/VECU communication issue, not a pedal hardware fault.

When detected, the engine defaults to idle-only to prevent runaway. Truck may still start but won't accept throttle.

Diagnose J1939 bus health first (SPN 639 related codes). Check cab harness connectors and pedal pigtail.

fixSteps.title: Check pedal connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and reseat. Inspect pins for corrosion or bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Check J1939
fixSteps.instruction: Measure CAN termination (~60Ω) at 9-pin port. Look for concurrent bus codes.

fixSteps.title: Dealer VECU diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If bus and pedal check out, VECU likely. Dealer-level replacement and programming.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo VNL throttle pedal J1939 SPN 974

faq.a: Yes — lost throttle data defaults to idle to prevent unintended acceleration.
Could be, but 9 = data link, not sensor. Check bus first.

title: EGR Valve Voltage Low
shortDescription: EGR valve actuator circuit shorted to ground.
fullDescription:
SPN 2791 FMI 4 on Volvo D11/D13/D16 engines indicates the EGR valve actuator circuit voltage is below normal — typically a shorted actuator coil or a harness shorted to ground.

With EGR disabled, NOx rises and SCR efficiency codes will follow. Also typically causes black smoke and power loss depending on strategy.

Harness inspection near the exhaust manifold is critical — heat damage is common.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Trace EGR harness, look for heat melt or chafe near exhaust manifold.

fixSteps.title: Measure coil
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect actuator, measure resistance. Short (near 0Ω) confirms coil failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator / harness
fixSteps.instruction: Swap actuator, repair harness with solder and heat shrink. Use heat sleeve in manifold area.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 EGR valve SPN 2791 FMI 4

faq.a: Yes — factory sleeves degrade, aftermarket sleeves prevent recurrence.
Volvo Tech Tool EGR calibration recommended.

title: Oil Pressure Moderately Low
shortDescription: Oil pressure below normal but above critical — investigate before it drops further.
fullDescription:
SPN 100 FMI 18 on Volvo D11/D13/D16 indicates oil pressure in the moderately-low range — worse than FMI 17 warning, but not yet FMI 1 (critical shutdown).

Check oil level first, then mechanical gauge. Volvo D13 known for oil dilution from injector cup leaks — check oil for fuel smell. Dilution thins oil, drops pressure, accelerates wear.

Ignoring progresses to FMI 1 with immediate engine protection shutdown.

fixSteps.title: Check oil
fixSteps.instruction: Level and condition. Smell for diesel (dilution). Top off to full.

fixSteps.title: Mechanical gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm actual pressure with mechanical gauge vs ECM reading. If mechanical OK, sensor fault.

fixSteps.title: Injector cup inspection
fixSteps.instruction: If oil diluted, Volvo dealer inspects injector cups for leaks. Cup replacement is major job.

whenToCallPro: If dilution or internal fault — dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 oil dilution SPN 100 FMI 18

faq.a: Volvo D13 injector cup issue is well-documented — check if oil smells of fuel.
$3,000-$6,000 depending on cup count and shop rate.

title: Starter Relay Circuit Voltage High
shortDescription: Starter control circuit voltage above normal — wiring or relay fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 677 FMI 3 on Volvo VN/VNL indicates the starter relay control circuit voltage is higher than expected — typically an open wire, bad relay, or wiring rubbed against 12V source.

Truck may crank erratically, not crank, or occasionally crank when key returns from start. A stuck starter solenoid from this fault can damage the flywheel ring gear.

Diagnose starter relay and harness before starter motor replacement.

fixSteps.title: Swap relay
fixSteps.instruction: Swap starter relay with an identical one in the fuse panel as a test.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Trace starter signal wire from ignition switch to starter. Measure for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Replace starter if solenoid fault
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring clear and relay good, starter solenoid is likely.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo VNL starter relay SPN 677 FMI 3

faq.a: Relay is $20 vs starter $500 — always swap relay first.
Stuck solenoid keeps starter engaged — grinds gear.

title: Aftertreatment SCR Catalyst Face Plugged
shortDescription: SCR catalyst face plugged with urea crystals or ash — flow restricted.
fullDescription:
SPN 4363 FMI 2 on Volvo D11/D13/D16 indicates the SCR catalyst is showing erratic/blocked behavior — often urea crystal deposits on the face or internal flow restriction.

Usually caused by a faulty doser spraying improperly (dribble instead of mist) or chronic low exhaust temperatures. Crystal buildup can be partially cleared with sustained high-temperature operation or dealer thermal service.

Severe cases require SCR replacement — $6,000+. Prevention: healthy doser + adequate exhaust temperature operation.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose doser
fixSteps.instruction: Test DEF doser spray pattern with Volvo Tech Tool. Replace if dribbling.

fixSteps.title: Sustained highway operation
fixSteps.instruction: Run truck at highway speed 1-2 hours to attempt burn-off of crystals.

fixSteps.title: Dealer SCR service
fixSteps.instruction: If crystals persist, dealer offers thermal service or replacement.

videoSearchQuery: Volvo D13 SCR plugged SPN 4363 urea crystal

faq.a: Sometimes — sustained 1100°F+ SCR face temp can burn off crystals.
